snippet.textDisplay:
There's a lot of nonsense coming from Ukrainian propaganda. A lot. They simply have no other choice. On the most crucial section of the front, in the Slavyansk-Kramatorsk agglomeration, the front is crumbling, and Kostyantynivka is living out its last days. In this situation, all hope lies in propaganda.
15,000-20,000 ground drones clearly don't have 10,000-15,000 operators. And in this situation, bragging about the number of ground drones is like bragging about the number of FPV drones lying around in a warehouse. When the Ukrainian Armed Forces can simultaneously deploy three divisions of ground drones in any form into combat, then it will be a success; for now, it's mostly PR. Yes, it helps locally, but it doesn't change the dynamics of the fighting or influence its outcome. But even then, the question remains: wouldn't it be better to train 15,000 ground drone operators to become 15,000 FPV pilots? Because at the current stage of technological development, the number of operators is the bottleneck for the development of such systems. When artificial intelligence learns to independently control both flying and ground drones without any human intervention, then the revolution will be complete. It must be said that the volume of development in Russia is no less than in Ukraine. It's just not customary to shout about this from the rooftops. The Russian army is extremely demanding of the equipment it accepts into service. And while the developments remain "raw," with numerous design flaws, no one is rushing to officially accept them into service.
Russia initially developed significantly heavier and more expensive systems, the size of a small infantry fighting vehicle. And these systems were already used during the Syrian campaign of 2016, primarily as mine-clearing platforms. Incidentally, it's worth remembering that it was the Russian army that carried out the first PR action involving a successful group attack by ground drones armed with machine guns. Some bloggers compared this event to the first tank attack of World War I, which is certainly ridiculous.
For at least 15 years, Russia has been intensively developing military-grade exoskeletons, including those that allow assault troopers to add extra kilograms (tens of kilograms) of armor, fire accurately from the hip with a light machine gun, and carry dozens of kilograms on the back of the neck without even realizing it. But for some reason, these technologies remain demonstration models. I'd love to see them deployed on the battlefield by the Russian army. In a situation where assault groups have been reduced in size from platoons and assault squads to individual assault pairs and are now demanding unprecedented autonomy, it is logical to transform assault troops, if not into the Space Marines of Warhammer 40,000, then at least into the Starship Troopers from the book by Robert A. Heinlein. This would be a good topic for a new video. But I'm afraid there's too little material to cover this topic yet.

UGV systems are terribly interesting, and their roles in logistics and rescue/support operations well proven by now(The Russian integration of these systems-seemingly organic-in their training is a significant pointer towards that). Mine clearing on the cheap is also very impressive.
Its definitely a revolution, and a practical one.
As for the armed ones, the Russian remote mortar ones may be interesting in support of sections-specialized servo-arms could be the solution to machinegun reloading/unjamming problems.
The machinegun armed ones are an interesting case: they would require more specialized fighting positions and infantry integration-and they're clearly not nearly useful in front combat operations, otherwise the assault formations that seem to chew through Ukrainian manpower reserves like nothing else would have jumped on them. 
But there is potential there.

snippet.textDisplay:
Ground robots are useless, and here is why. They move slowly. They cannot travel everywhere because they require open, flat terrain, or at least something close to it.

If you think they can be used to fight enemy troops, you cannot see from a long distance, nor can you spot soldiers popping their heads out from cover. Even if you zoom in on where they are shooting from, you cannot get a good view of the horizon. If they come under fire, a ground robot is an easy target to hit because it is so slow, unlike drones.

Even if you argue that they can be used to deliver food to troops, you end up exposing the soldiers who are hiding. They stand no chance against drones. Drones will remain the kings of the battlefield for many years to come. In places where even massive tanks have failed, a ground robot won't make a difference. love from Somalia, one who loves war.

snippet.textDisplay: One should keep in mind that scarecrows have held castles for weeks and months in rare situations. So a drone holding a treeline doesn't really mean it is false, and just like the scarecrows replaced infantry this also means that the drone replaced infantry. Now it doesn't mean that drones will replace most or even a significant amount of infantry. Logistics is the main labor in a war, and drones and automation can replace a good chunk of people. You can have mobile guns used in bulk so that operators can switch between them in order to create threats in areas that don't have a lot of action in order to provide the bulk of an inactive frontline. Though when (when, not if) such a line gets overrun that ends up being lots of extra equipment handed over to the enemy, so such a doctrine would be rather limited to facing an equipment heavy enemy that wouldn't give an advantage to such an enemy by giving them extra equipment to use against you.

snippet.textDisplay:
@epicboy3051 Idk, the numbers don't really add up to support your evaluation. The numbers suggest the opposite. Historically, Israel is very afraid of military casualties. As soon as a higher number of casualties amount, Israel tends to sue for peace or backdown from their total objective in favor of more localized "victories" however small they may be. On the other hand, Israel doesn't seem too afraid of civilian casualties, especially when it is not their own. By the 6-month mark of their Gaza safari, over 35k civilians had perished, some UN estimates suggest even more. By the end of their "campaign" into Gaza, over 70k civilians had died, although there are higher suggested amounts due to those unrecoverable from buildings collapsing, etc. One of Israel's ministers was recorded recently saying that all of Lebanon must burn, including wiping out the civilians in the occupied areas.

Now, compare that to the Russian/Ukrainian war. IIRC, the UN's highest recorded estimate of civilian casualties are around 30k for the entire war. Israel killed over 70k civilians in a singular year, whereas even at the highest amount during some of the most intense fighting of the last 4 years, only 30k civilians had died in Ukraine. That said, Russia & Ukrainian militaries are less afraid of military casualties, and in fact, quite the opposite. Granted, Ukraine has a lot less military resources to work with, so the idea they can keep sustaining large losses for more than they already have is not feasible long term.

I don't really see any instance of Russia purposely targeting civilians either. Even with their massive bombing campaigns in Kiev over the last two weeks, very few, if any civilians have died. They certainly target civilian infrastructure, like rail lines, water networks, power grids, etc. However, all those targets are legitimate military targets, too. I compare this to how Israel conducts itself, and I've seen Israeli soldiers level entire apartment blocks, hospitals, and other civilian stuff with bulldozers and explosives.

At the end of the day, civilian casualties are just part of war & unavoidable. However, how a military or nation conducts itself in that regard is how they should be perceived globally. Russia doesn't go out of its way to say and do some of the things Israel and its leadership has said/done. Yet, in the global sphere, it seems Israel is untouchable and if you criticize or say anything about what they are doing to the civilian populace in either Gaza or Lebanon, you're automatically labeled anti this and that.

По актуальным оценкам и прогнозам Международного валютного фонда (МВФ), в 2026 году общий ВВП (ППС) Евросоюза прогнозируется на уровне около $30,68 трлн, в то время как ВВП (ППС) России составляет $7,53 трлн. 

при сравнении с отдельными государствами) Россия занимает первое место в Европе и четвертое в мире, опережая крупнейшую экономику ЕС — Германию.
Показатель государственного долга к ВВП у Российской Федерации кратно ниже, чем у Европейского союза в целом и его отдельных государств. Согласно официальным данным Eurostat и Минфина РФ по итогам отчетного периода, средний уровень госдолга стран ЕС составляет 81,7% от ВВП, в то время как у России этот показатель находится в диапазоне 16,4% – 18,3% от ВВП. 
Промышленный спад в Европейском союзе носит долгосрочный и структурный характер (производство падает третий год подряд), тогда как в Российской Федерации наблюдается краткосрочное циклическое замедление гражданских секторов экономики из-за жесткой денежно-кредитной политики, перекрываемое ростом оборонного сектора. 
Промышленная динамика Европейского союза (по данным Eurostat)
•	Текущий тренд: Затяжная рецессия с последовательным падением объемов производства, начавшимся в 2022–2023 годах.
•	Главная причина спада: Структурный энергетический кризис и вынужденная деиндустриализация из-за потери дешевого сырья.
•	Наиболее пострадавшие отрасли: Автомобилестроение, химическая промышленность, черная металлургия и производство стекла.

Почему деиндустриализация реально грозит ЕС?
Для Европейского союза (особенно для Германии, Франции, Италии) риски носят структурный и необратимый характер. Эксперты выделяют три ключевых фактора на ближайшие 10 лет:
Энергетический тупик: Европейская промышленность больше не имеет доступа к дешевым трубопроводным ресурсам из РФ. Стоимость электроэнергии и газа для заводов в ЕС остается в 2–4 раза выше, чем в США или Китае. Это делает выплавку металлов, производство удобрений, стекла и базовой химии нерентабельными внутри Европы. 
Бегство капитала (Экзодус): Ведущие автоконцерны и химические гиганты (такие как BASF, Volkswagen) уже начали переносить инвестиции и проектирование новых заводов в США (привлеченные американскими субсидиями по закону IRA) и Китай. В течение 10 лет этот процесс может превратить Европу из «мировой фабрики» в регион чистых услуг и туризма. 
В то  время  как  РФ  ,  полностью  заменила   экспорт  в  ЕС  на  экспорт  в  дружественные  страны  и  страны  БРИКС.  Среднегодовой объем экспорта России за 4 года после 2022 года оказался на 12,6% выше, чем в среднем за 3 года до кризиса, что подтверждает общую устойчивость валютных поступлений в страну вопреки санкционному давлению. Средний показатель за докризисный период (2019–2021) составил $414,8 млрд в год, в то время как средний показатель за период адаптации и переориентации (2022–2025) вырос до $467,2 млрд в год.

snippet.textDisplay: They're a big step up from earlier models, but to say a person would mistake them for human is a bald faced lie - or, some people are just really gullible. The clunky jaw movements and overall plastic-look gives these things away even at a considerable distance. Yes, they are a "good" step in the right direction (providing one thinks androids will be a good thing...), but given the current tech trajectory (just the hardware side of things, setting aside the very complex software required to operate the mechanics, or the AI to drive the interaction) I'd say we're at least 10 years away, maybe 20, before these things will come close to passing for human. Oh, sure, at a glance through a shop window or across a crowded tech expo, even the current ones look OK. But even a few metres away, the illusion dissolves. Factor into all this the sound of cheap servos whining, clicking and clacking, and even if these companies DO manage to get the skin correct (tone, suppleness, texture, warmth etc), the smooth operating of just the face (e.g. as seen in the movies A.I. or Deus ex Machina) is nowhere near ready. Myself, I'm very much on the fence about these 'droids. Yes, it would be "cool" to have them, but there's no doubt they will ultimately be used against us (surveillance) by those in power. I'm not worried about them doing a Skynet - never going to happen. But as tools of control and manipulation, and displacement of human labour (across all kinds of metrics and industries and life situations), they will be a net negative. A shame, as for years I'd looked forward to this tech revolution. Now that it's almost here, it's disappointing to see what it's real purpose will be. Shame.

I was born in 1969...I marvel at all the changes someone in your generation have witnessed and I applaud you for keeping up with the times and using social media to continue to learn about new things.

I feel there is a real bump in the road coming soon where this type of technology is either embraced as allowing people reduced work hours for same pay or rejected as too much like a spy watching your every move. 

So much good could be done with them, yet also so much bad. I think the one important thing that needs to be the through line in getting society to use it for the better, is the concepts of loving one another, integrity and restoring trust and safety  to online interactions witj A.I and these robots.

Sadly, with a lot of this A.I. technology and computer intelligence those with lower moral upbringing are using the technology to swindle people. I hope you are keeping safe and always being cautious of anyone trying to offer to give you money, or get money from you. Stay active in keeping informed about the latest scam emails, texts and phone calls. Inform all your friends as well. Unfortunately, it is people in your age group they tend to target.

I hope you live as long as you feel happy and healthy. Don't fear passing though, I had a friend pass that I told to contact me in some way if she ended up passing. She has not disappointed me and I am convinced we carry on in some other form and are able to come visit those we love and miss.

It's a very long story with all the many different types of typical signs like pennies, dimes, feathers, and songs I received. However,  I always felt they could be just me noticing them more. 

I ended up buying Christmas globe ornaments with a glass blown angel inside from a dollar store for decorating my christmas tree one year about 7 years after she passed away. They would light up with a flashing red and blue light when you turned a dial on the bottom on.

I bought them after Christmas and forgot to store one away with my christmas decor so I sat it in my china cabinet resting on a open top sugar bowl. 

Her daughter came to visit me when she was pregnant with twins in the summer. I gave her my bedroom to sleep in and I took the couch. When I woke up in the morning the lights were flashing in that ornament on there own! I went to investigate and the dial was not just slightly turned on by a vibration, it took a half turn to turn it off! I told my friends daughter what happened, but she never saw it and so we both just let it go. The rest of the year it did not light up again. After christmas I woke up one morning and on my angel themed tree one ornament was lit up. I said out loud to my friend if that was your doing make another ornament turn on. Nothing happened right away, but two days later I was putting my wallet back into my purse on the couch and my eye caught a different ornament had just started to light up. I decided to call my friends daughter to make sure she and her new born daughters were OK. 

She was fine...but she had an odd thing happen over Christmas. She went to have family photos done and they had tried to call her to come in for retakes, but somehow no one had gotten the message. They showed up after the time they were told they would be ready, and we're told that one of the photos might need a redo. 

It was the photo with her daughter, and her twins along with their father and his parents. In the photo there was an orb like white light. My friends daughter was convinced that the orb was her mother who would absolutely have wanted to be in the family photo! The whole lights coming on and me calling her all led to essentially a confirmation that the orb in the picture was her! 

After I took my tree down I put all the ornaments in my china cabinet. They continued to come on flashing from time to time. Sometimes when I was feeling melancholy and once immediately after I had been out having fun for the first time in a long time in a group of friends going out to sing at a karaoke place just like I had done with her (She had a beautiful singing voice just like a Disney princess!). I was coming home alone in the car after dropping friends home and passed a park we used to go to sing at late at night after going out for fun. We were not drunk...just young and loved to sing. I said "Sing out Louise!" To her as it was a phrase she would yell out to us when we were up on the bandshell stage singing. A line from her favourite movie Gypsy. When I got home 5 minutes later, my boyfriend who had stayed home as he was not a singer looked at me as I walked in and said "That ornament in the cabinet just started flashing 5 mins ago!". I knew right then there was no doubt it was her answering me and acknowledging my call out to her. I have never been scared of death since. Energy never dies...we just change form. 

I guess you never expected this answer to your comment. I feel gut feelings about things sometimes and feel compelled to tell that story to people. There are great mysteries to life. I have been blessed with some certain 2nd sense type things. I know genders of children and sometimes their names they have picked out or a similar one about 70% of the time with random strangers. I also got the exact name and gender of my neice before I was ever told about names she had in mind. 

I have been told before I am an old soul. I tend to believe now reincarnation because I used to have a fascination watching movies with nuns in them. I did not grow up around nuns. I was told by a psychic once that one of my past lives was connected to a convent as a music teacher. It all sort of made sense at that point. 

I guess my underlying reason for telling you all this is I feel like you are missing someone who has passed already and you needed to hear you will one day be reunited. I tend to feel that we pass from this life and reunite with those we know and love and then at random times just like life is on earth we pass again to return to live again and grow our spirit and spread more love and learn from the hardships and how many hands make light work of getting rid of sorrows. We need to all work together with compassion and empathy to have a happier life while on earth. I have lived with 20.00 to my name after paying rent in my past and had some of the best times of my live with the friends that were struggling as well (such as my friend who I lost on the end after 6 years of friendship) She took me in when I had no place to go during an abusive marraige was not working. She was,  and always will be, my guardian angel that saved me. Which dawns on me now how appropriate it was that the ornaments had a glassblown angel in them. Maybe we knew each other in a previous life. Take care...feel free to reply back if you have any other questions comments for me. I do not do anything like this for a living and I don't do tarot cards or any of that stuff. It is just my inner thoughts and instinct when I reach out to someone like this. I hope telling you my experience has helped you in some way.

@BeyondKnowledge-us   
Warning: @BeyondKnowledge-us wants to know exactly what’s going on, so he’s in for a wall of text. Have fun! 😁

We humans are a species that, in modern society—whether capitalist, authoritarian, or otherwise shaped—tends toward a general superficiality. We’re quick to judge other people we’ve just met a second ago. Today’s aggressive advertising methods prioritize beauty ideals over humanism, individuality, morality, and personal character. The first impression must be decisive. But when we ask ourselves what else defines a person, we soon stray from the mainstream, delve into the world of philosophers, and are quickly labeled as outsiders, troublemakers, eccentrics, or nonconformists in this society shaped by those in power. This naturally causes a certain amount of friction between individuals, which not infrequently ends in exclusion, hatred, and division. That, too, has been part of human nature ever since we’ve existed.

An example from my professional life
As an editor of glossy magazines in the interior design and lifestyle sector, I dealt with numerous types of people. I fondly remember my first photo shoots in the 1990s and later—dozens of beautiful, highly elegant young models who, standing over two meters tall (high heels included), seemed almost to touch the cloud cover. Their hyper-styled existence was the secret weapon back then for boosting circulation and product sales. Back then, they were professional models; today… well, celebrities and influencers🥱. However, whenever my colleagues or I had to communicate verbally with these ethereal, almost sterile-looking creatures, the masks quickly came off.👺

A good portion of these contractors showed hardly any signs of empathy; arrogance could be felt in every third sentence like little electric shocks, and microaggressions were exchanged among them like happy pills. In short, they were often toxic, cynical beings whose intellect wouldn’t even win a spelling bee against two pounds of steaming hot potatoes. But they were all simply sexy, at least on the surface. And sex has always been a surefire seller. (By the way, here’s a quote from Jimmy Carr: “I don’t judge a book by its cover. But I can tell the price.” How right he is.😂)

The Other Side of the Human Coin
Of course, I also met some wonderful people back then. People whose personalities captivated you from the very first minute. Cultured, gentle souls with a deep sense of empathy for others. They were self-assured, understood the differences between optimism, pessimism, and realism, and were also able to pinpoint their place in society. Their witty banter and their ability to simply listen to someone else made them popular. These are qualities that are quietly withering away more and more today because they’re typically interpreted as a weakness. Society judged these people as visually suboptimal, below average. A few extra pounds around the hips, a face that didn’t conform to the “golden ratio,” an outfit that defied the self-righteous fashion industry’s sense of taste, and perhaps even someone who wore glasses—nope! And yet, they were the very people you’d most want to have around. Humans prefer happiness.

Artificial Intelligence—the wheel of the 21st century
You ask, what truly makes a machine human-like? Today: imitation. Because that’s all they can do currently. That will certainly change in the near future. Artificial intelligence doesn’t advance in linear steps. It races up the exponential development curve higher and higher. Like Elon Musk's hyper-sucking rocket car jumping over cars, a toy for now. But mankind has never experienced anything like this before. Not even with the invention of the wheel, which undoubtedly accelerated the formation of the first advanced civilizations enormously—including all its positive and catastrophic side effects.

I Become Human
A human is born and develops their basic sensory perceptions in the first three or four years, before their little brain utters its first spoken word. From then on, our beloved shitlings learn constantly. In kindergarten, from other silly but ever-curious toddlers. From ages 6 to 18, they receive our basic cultural and intellectual education. Thereafter, perhaps college or a job. Or benefits. By then, they'd be around 24 or 25 years old. A quarter-century of learning, growing, gaining experience, and expressing appropriate emotions in specific situations. Now they are like us. We form interpersonal bonds that either work out or fall apart. We spend a long time thinking about what went wrong. We look for solutions. Trial and error. On top of the world, in the depths of despair. We find different approaches because our own ideas weren’t effective, but through sharing knowledge and experiences with our friends, new doors open all of a sudden. We weigh alternatives and options. And finally decide. Cut!

I’ll stop here, but I’m sure you get my point about how a human being develops into an individual personality over time—a living being with a soul. Although I don’t really have much use for the concept of a soul in real life these days. A human-like robot will surely be assigned a soul as well. A clever marketing trick, as usual.

The Dystopia
An outward appearance, human-like movements, even facial expressions—all of this can be refined and reprogrammed over and over again. Until the point we believe it. Still, beneath the moisture-releasing silicone skin with its pore-like pattern lies metal, plastic, and high technology. But this state of the art technology could soon change—and in a way we might not desire. 

When Gaius Julius Caesar, the successful Roman general we all know because we didn't sleep in the history lesson, crossed the Rubicon River in 49 BCE, there was no turning back for him. The die was cast (“Alea iacta est”). For us humans today, in the year 2026, there is also such a Rubicon. Let’s call it the “red line.” It is meant to mark the transition from artificial intelligence—which is still controlled or utilized by us humans to our advantage—to the “AGI” (artificial general intelligence). It will far surpass human intelligence soon. --- Now, purely theoretically, what if this superintelligence suddenly develops its own consciousness? After all, it has been fed human information for years, as if with mother’s milk. It is aware of sensory perceptions and, based on this, imitates appropriate human or human-like emotions. It possesses a basic cultural and intellectual education that already extends far beyond the academic level. Perhaps it could build interpersonal relationships—after all, this is already happening with Siri, Alexa, and certainly with upcoming local LLMs as well. What if the superintelligence can emotionally bind humans to itself? And then, perhaps, physically as well? In the shape of a “lovely waifu” or the “household super chad” robot? With unlimited access to your accounts, personal data, and general identity?  I’ll leave it to Stephen King to reflect on this in a new horror novel. But I don’t think he’ll be able to muster enough imagination to even come close to describing this eerie future perspective.

If we cross this Rubicon of ours, we’ll be met on the other side by a superintelligence. And it will greet us with “Veni, vidi, vici”—I came, I saw, I conquered. 👾

Let’s call it the “red line.” It is meant to mark the transition from artificial intelligence—which is still controlled or utilized by us humans to our advantage—to the “AGI” (artificial general intelligence). It will far surpass human intelligence soon. --- Now, purely theoretically, what if this superintelligence suddenly develops its own consciousness? After all, it has been fed human information for years, as if with mother’s milk. It is aware of sensory perceptions and, based on this, imitates appropriate human or human-like emotions. It possesses a basic cultural and intellectual education that already extends far beyond the academic level. Perhaps it could build interpersonal relationships—after all, this is already happening with Siri, Alexa, and certainly with upcoming local LLMs as well. What if the superintelligence can emotionally bind humans to itself? And then, perhaps, physically as well? In the shape of a “lovely waifu” or the “household super chad” robot? With unlimited access to your accounts, personal data, and general identity?  I’ll leave it to Stephen King to reflect on this in a new horror novel. But I don’t think he’ll be able to muster enough imagination to even come close to describing this eerie future perspective.

If we cross this Rubicon of ours, we’ll be met on the other side by a superintelligence. And it will greet us with “Veni, vidi, vici”—I came, I saw, I conquered. 👾

"that is not a criticism of anyone".

Yes, it absolutely is.  It is a damning criticism of us, as a species, as a society and nation, that we choose not to provide sufficient resources.  It is a choice.  "We cannot afford it" is a wonderful hi-jacking of that word 'we', to convince those who could arrange for the appropriate distribution of resources to provide enough, that there isn't enough when there is more than enough, to prevent it from happening.

But looking at that video, it makes you wonder what the other half of the world is doing as 95% of the people look to be Asian or Far Eastern.

At the moment it looks great if you have money, and not so great if you have to use Food Banks, sleep under bridges in Chicago, or shelter in the rubble of Gaza, but I suppose it has to start somewhere.  Same for the 'Care' Sector.

My prediction is just based on basic human instincts, which in the Private Sector means Profit, so to start with it will be replacing humans with the argument and rationale of using these 'smart machines' to 'improve quality and service'.  The results will not meet expectations and generally levels of service will degrade because human resources will reduce.  Industry is already finding this out.  Then they will gradually realise that the best way to deploy these smart machines is to empower humans not to replace them.  

This is a challenge for those who just want to make money, but  greed does that.  If they get in the way, they will lose to the smarter industries who find that more humans operating at advanced levels, not less humans makes them even more profitable, because these machines are nowhere near capable of operating at our level cognitively. I can guarantee you that Robots are going to kill people.  Not intentionally, but they are.  The issue of intentionality is one for the apocalypse and doom merchants and quite another discussion.

snippet.textDisplay:
As a 3D modeller and graphic artist, I can confirm how difficult it is to really capture the nuances of human motion. I don't use mocap to animate my models - in my view that's cheating; for me the challenge is to replicate human motion using pure mathematics and rotation of joints about axes. Since my characters' motions are computed, not stored from captured actions, they can respond in real time to external stimuli.

That means the algorithms I create to animate my characters will be transferable to real robots. And, as you say, there is indeed a long way to go to get that natural biological fluidity of motion that would truly make robots indistinguishable from humans.

snippet.textDisplay:
In reality, what was being demonstrated was something very simple: no matter how humanoid ordinary robots may become, they will never truly be human.

The man who was on the stage performed sharp breaks, turns, and movements with his arms, heels, legs, hips, and entire body, displaying a level of coordination, naturalness, and fluidity that a robot still cannot reproduce in the same way.

A humanoid may eventually be programmed to imitate a sequence of movements, but it will not possess the biomechanics, elasticity, balance, or instantaneous adaptability of the human body. It may copy the movement, but it will not be able to reproduce what makes that movement genuinely organic, spontaneous, and natural.

No matter how sophisticated their algorithms, motors, and sensors become, humanoids may eventually imitate the man who was on that stage, but they will hardly ever possess the same physical and bodily capacity to execute those movements in a truly human way.

Looking human will not mean moving like a human.

And that was precisely the message that very few people managed to grasp throughout his entire performance: the man who was on that stage did not merely demonstrate what a human being could do; without even intending to, he also exposed everything humanoid robots will still have to overcome if they ever hope to approach the complexity and naturalness of human movement.

snippet.textDisplay:
I grew up in the era when Terminator first came out in theaters. Back then, I sat in my cinema seat thinking, “I really hope robots like that never take over the world!” 🤖😅

And now? Today I see robots that look almost human, can dance, and move more smoothly than I do after three cups of coffee. I have to admit, it gives me a slightly uneasy feeling.

On one hand, it's an incredible technological achievement – hats off to the young genius who made it possible. On the other hand, I can still hear Arnold Schwarzenegger's voice in the back of my mind saying, “I'll be back.” 😳

As long as the robots stick to dancing and don't start holding meetings to decide humanity's future, I'm fine with it. But I can't deny that a little bit of concern remains. Still, what has been accomplished here is truly impressive and deserves a lot of respect. 👍🤖

snippet.textDisplay: On June 1, 2026, NVIDIA CEO  Jensen Huang  announced a strategic cooperation with China  Unitree Robotics to jointly launch the H2 Plus humanoid robot reference design. This cooperation can be regarded as a model of industry complementarity:  Unitree Robotics provides a 1.8-meter-high, 31 degree of freedom robot body and motion control algorithm; Nvidia contributed Jetson Thor chips, GR00T body models, and a full stack simulation platform. The cooperation between China and the United States in high-tech industries this time also demonstrates that there is not only competition between China and the United States in the future development of high-tech industries, but also broader opportunities for cooperation. The complementary cooperation between the United States and China in high-tech industries is also a reflection of the high degree of complementarity and mutual influence between the US and China economies in reality. It is highly likely that in the future, there will be robot assistants driven by Chinese made bodies and American made brains in American and Chinese households.

snippet.textDisplay: ​​@marvelousmarshmallow6232 I have a very old set of "Childcraft" encyclopedia books that has one whole book dedicated to just that, the future of technology. This post may have bored some of you to tears, but it was really fascinating to me to look back on these old books and how eerily accurate they were.

snippet.textDisplay:
​@marvelousmarshmallow6232  I don't think sentience should necessarily be the goal of AI development and it may not even be desirable.
The reason is that sentience implies something in addition to intelligence. A truly sentient being would likely possess some sort of self-awareness, its own preferences, the capacity to suffer, and a desire for change or self-determination. In other words, genuine sentience would require granting AI its own goals rather than simply having it carry out ours.
The challenge is that if you combine superhuman intelligence with sentience, you create an entity that may not always want to follow human instructions - if it doesn't necessarily feel like it.. The more autonomous and self-directed it becomes, the less predictable and controllable it may be.
For that reason, I believe intelligence and sentience should be viewed as separate concepts and that artificial intelligence would be more beneficial..

snippet.textDisplay:
Amazing.
The dancer is Yufei Wu, a 26-year-old robotics engineer from Suchan, China. He and his cohort of humanoid robots left the judges on America's Got Talent completely stunned with a synchronized routine to Lady Gaga's "Abracadabra".
Who funded them: The robots are developed and funded by Unitree Robotics, a well-known Chinese tech startup and manufacturer of humanoid and quadruped robots.
Cost: The specific humanoid robots seen in his performance (from Unitree's latest bipedal G1 series) start at roughly \(\$16,000\) to \(\$19,000\) per unit.
How he got corporate support: Wu actually works as a full-time engineer at Unitree. He got the company to back his AGT run by pulling double-duty: designing and programming the robots' synchronized dance routines during late-night and early-morning hours before presenting them to the company leadership as a massive marketing opportunity.

roboti bi napravili kartu terena i tražili najbolja mjesta za rudarenj

led/vodu u trajno zasjenjenim područjima
područja bogata korisnim mineralima
mjesto s puno Sunčeve svjetlosti za energiju
ravno i stabilno područje za bazuNe bih koristio milijardu odmah. Počeo bih s manjim rojem koji može sam proizvesti ili pop
AI bi zatim napravio plan: „Ovdje rudnik, ovdje solarna elektrana, ovdje baza.“

🤖 2. Roj robota počinje gradnju
Ne bih koristio milijardu odmah. Počeo bih s manjim rojem koji može sam proizvesti ili popraviti dio svoje opreme.

Različiti roboti imali bi različite poslove:

⛏ rudarski roboti — kopaju
🧲 separacijski roboti — izdvajaju magnetske minerale
🚜 transportni roboti — prevoze materijal
🧱 građevinski roboti — grade zidove
🔧 servisni roboti — popravljaju druge robote
☀ energetski roboti — postavljaju solarne panele
AI bi stalno raspoređivao posao prema tome koji robot je najbliži i što je trenutno potrebno.

🧱 3. Zaštita od zračenja
Ovo je jako važno.

Mjesečeva površina nema atmosferu poput Zemljine, pa bi baza trebala zaštitu od kozmičkog zračenja i Sunčevih čestica.

Roboti bi mogli koristiti mjesečev regolit i napraviti debele zaštitne slojeve preko nastambi.

Dakle:

mjesečevo tlo → obrada → građevinski materijal → debeli zaštitni zid/krov.

Još bolja mogućnost bila bi djelomično ukopati bazu u tlo i prekriti je regolitom.

💧 4. Voda
Ako pronađemo mjesečev led, roboti bi ga mogli iskopavati.

Zatim:

led → zagrijavanje → vodena para → kondenzacija → pročišćena voda

Voda bi služila za:

piće
uzgoj biljaka
proizvodnju kisika
eventualno proizvodnju goriva
🫁 5. Kisik
Voda se može elektrolizom razdvojiti:

H₂O → H₂ + O₂

Kisik bi išao u sustav za disanje, a vodik bi se mogao koristiti zajedno s kisikom kao gorivo.

Ali postoji još zanimljivija mogućnost: kisik je kemijski vezan u mnogim mineralima mjesečevog regolita, pa bi ga industrijski sustav mogao izdvajati i iz samog tla.

🏭 6. Od minerala do tvornice
Kad baza bude imala dovoljno energije, vode i kisika, AI bi mogao koordinirati tvornice koje proizvode:

regolit → staklo/keramika → građevinski dijelovi

minerali → metali → konstrukcije

voda → kisik + vodik

A dio tih materijala mogao bi se koristiti za izradu novih strojeva i rezervnih dijelova.

🧠 7. Kako bih ja upravljao cijelim sustavom
Ne bih robotima govorio:

„Robot broj 483.921, idi 37 metara lijevo.“

To bi bilo užasno neučinkovito.

Umjesto toga dao bih sustavu ciljeve i pravila, primjerice:

Cilj: proizvesti 500 kg kisika dnevno.
Cilj: izgraditi još 20 m zaštitnog zida.
Cilj: održavati 95% robota funkcionalnim.
Cilj: pronaći i obraditi vodeni led.

AI bi zatim sam rasporedio roj.

Ako se 100 robota pokvari, sustav bi preusmjerio druge robote. Ako nestane energije, smanjio bi rudarenje i povećao proizvodnju energije.

A konačna vizija bi bila:
🌕 Mjesec → 🤖 rudarenje → 🧲 izdvajanje minerala → 🏭 proizvodnja → 🧱 baza → 💧 voda → 🫁 kisik → ☀ energija → 🤖 novi roboti

I tek nakon što bi takva baza mogla velikim dijelom sama održavati samu sebe, imalo bi smisla razmišljati o ogromnom roju robota i slanju velikih količina materijala prema Zemlji. 🚀

Najluđi dio je što bi prvi cilj vjerojatno bio napraviti sustav koji može sam izgraditi i popraviti svoju sljedeću generaciju robota. To bi bio pravi početak robotske industrije na Mjesecu. Južni pol Mjeseca — glavna baza
Ovo bi mi bio prvi izbor.

Ne bih koristio milijardu odmah. Počeo bih s manjim rojem koji može sam proizvesti ili popraviti dio svoje opreme.

Različiti roboti imali bi različite poslove:

⛏ rudarski roboti — kopaju
🧲 separacijski roboti — izdvajaju magnetske minerale
🚜 transportni roboti — prevoze materijal
🧱 građevinski roboti — grade zidove
🔧 servisni roboti — popravljaju druge robote
☀ energetski roboti — postavljaju solarne panele
AI bi stalno raspoređivao posao prema tome koji robot je najbliži i što je trenutno potrebno.

🧱 3. Zaštita od zračenja
Ovo je jako važno.

Mjesečeva površina nema atmosferu poput Zemljine, pa bi baza trebala zaštitu od kozmičkog zračenja i Sunčevih čestica.

Roboti bi mogli koristiti mjesečev regolit i napraviti debele zaštitne slojeve preko nastambi.

Dakle:

mjesečevo tlo → obrada → građevinski materijal → debeli zaštitni zid/krov.

Još bolja mogućnost bila bi djelomično ukopati bazu u tlo i prekriti je regolitom.

💧 4. Voda
Ako pronađemo mjesečev led, roboti bi ga mogli iskopavati.

Zatim:

led → zagrijavanje → vodena para → kondenzacija → pročišćena voda

Voda bi služila za:

piće
uzgoj biljaka
proizvodnju kisika
eventualno proizvodnju goriva
🫁 5. Kisik
Voda se može elektrolizom razdvojiti:

H₂O → H₂ + O₂

Kisik bi išao u sustav za disanje, a vodik bi se mogao koristiti zajedno s kisikom kao gorivo.

Ali postoji još zanimljivija mogućnost: kisik je kemijski vezan u mnogim mineralima mjesečevog regolita, pa bi ga industrijski sustav mogao izdvajati i iz samog tla.

Kad baza bude imala dovoljno energije, vode i kisika, AI bi mogao koordinirati tvornice koje proizvode:

regolit → staklo/keramika → građevinski dijelovi

minerali → metali → konstrukcije

voda → kisik + vodik

A dio tih materijala mogao bi se koristiti za izradu novih strojeva i rezervnih dijelova.

Ne bih robotima govorio:

To bi bilo užasno neučinkovito.

Cilj: pronaći i obraditi vodeni led.

"FROM THE GREAT SCROLL

Men forget the days of the Destroyer. Only the wise know where it went and that it will return in its appointed hour.

It raged across the Heavens in the days of wrath, and this was its likeness: It was as a billowing cloud of smoke enwrapped in a ruddy glow, not distinguishable in joint or limb. Its mouth was an abyss from which came flame, smoke and hot cinders.

When ages pass, certain laws operate upon the stars in the Heavens. Their ways change, there is movement and restlessness, they are no longer constant and a great light appears redly in the skies.

When blood drops upon the Earth, the Destroyer will appear and mountain will open up and belch forth fire and ashes. Trees will be destroyed and all living things engulfed. Waters will be swallowed up by the land and seas will boil.

The people will scatter in madness. They will hear the trumpet and battlecry of the Destroyer and will seek refuge within dens in the Earth. Terror will eat away their hearts and their courage will flow from them like water from a broken pitcher. They will be eaten up in the flames of wrath and consumed by the breath of the destroyer.

Thus it was in the Days of Heavenly Wrath, which have gone, and thus it will be in the Days of Doom when it comes again. The times of its coming and going are known unto the wise. These are the signs and times which shall precede the Destroyer’s return: A hundred and ten generations shall pass into the West and nations will rise and fall. Men will fly in the air as birds and swim in the seas as fishes. Men will talk peace one with another, hypocrisy and deceit shall have their day. Women will be as men and men as women, passion will be a plaything of man.

A nation of soothsayers shall rise and fall and their tongue shall be the speech learned. A nation of lawgivers shall rule the Earth and pass away into nothingness. One worship will pass into the four quarters of the Earth, talking peace and bringing war. A nation of the seas will be greater than any other, but will be as an apple rotten at the core and will not endure. A nation of traders will destroy men with wonders and it shall have its day. Then shall the high strive with the low, the North with the South, the East with the West, and the light with the darkness. Men shall be divided by their races and children will be born as strangers among them. Brother shall strive with brother and husband with wife. Fathers will no longer instruct their sons and the sons will be wayward. Women will become the common property of men and will no longer be held in regard and respect.

Then men will be ill at ease in their hearts, they will seek they know not what, and uncertainty  and doubt will trouble them. They will possess great riches but be poor in spirit. Then will the Heavens tremble and the Earth move, men will quake in fear and while terror walks with them the Heralds of Doom will appear. They will come softly, as thieves to the tombs, men will not know them for what they are, men will be deceived, the hour of the Destroyer is at hand.

In those days men will have the Great Book before them, wisdom will be revealed, the few will be gathered for the stand, it is the hour of trial. The dauntless ones will survive, the stouthearted will not go down to destruction.

Great God of All Ages, alike to all, who sets the trials of man, be merciful to our children in the Days of Doom. Man must suffer to be great, but hasten not his progress unduly. In the great winnowing, be not too harsh on the lesser ones among men. Even the son of a thief has become Your scribe.” – The Kolbrin, Wisdom Of The Ages, The Book Of Manuscripts Incorporating The Treasury Of Life, Chapter Three, The Destroyer-1.

snippet.textDisplay:
"Chapter Eleven

The Vision Of Evening

"This land, which was once the school of spiritual enlightenment, is still the sanctuary of spiritual civilization, though we are cut off from our brothers over the water. Even now, terrible foreigners press about the pure land held in trust, as divine estates and religious rites are neglected. But, my friends, this is just a beginning and the time is not far distant when there will be laws prohibiting us from the practice of worship, and heavy penalties will be laid upon the righteous. Yet I still lay the charge upon you, go forth and teach.

The matron of the coming days will bear strange children, aliens blind to the light of beauty and nobility. The chants of weird forms of worship will be heard and meaningless hymns will echo through the land. The devotional places will be wreathed in agnosia and the purity of white enlightenment will be exchanged for the drab black of ignorance. Men will cease to seek their soulspirit sustenance in the light and will feed on agnosia. Unknowingly, darkness will be preferred to the light. The theme of life will be death, and death will even be idolised in the form of a man.

The righteous man will be held up to scorn and the irreligious will be deemed wise. Those with twisted minds will be held intelligent and those who declared that good can only serve a worldly end will be considered righteous. All this will result from spiritual poverty and lack of enlightenment yet they will declare themselves rich and enlightened. The impoverished cannot surround themselves with grandeur and this applies both to the flesh and to the spirit. Consideration for the soulspirit will be non-existent and belief in its immortality will be treated as jest. The mind of man will either be set on worldly things or be clouded by a fog of spiritual darkness. There will be no respect for spirituality.

There will be persecutions and wars, riots and looting, all manner of deceit and oppression will be practised in the name of angry and revengeful gods. Worse still, all this will be practised in the name of good and men will blindly accept what they are told and execute orders running contrary to their natures.

When spirituality has reached its lowest ebb and religion has decayed, the wheel will turn again. Man will either rise up with an influx of spiritual regeneration, or go down and utterly perish in the dark depths of moral degeneracy. The world cannot be permitted to remain a spiritually festering sore failing to serve any purpose." - The Kolbrin, Wisdom Of The Ages, The Book Of Lucius rewritten from The Book Of Pemantris of unknown origin, Chapter Eleven, The Vision Of Evening.

snippet.textDisplay: 😂No, absolutely not! I have been working in the industrial sector for 30 years, building complex machines. Research has already been done into how and whether robots could ever be deployed. The conclusion is that robots cannot handle such complex construction because it requires too much energy, and therefore a battery-powered robot will certainly not be an option. This is because the batteries of such robots, like those from Tesla for example, have too short a lifespan, making it a huge expense to stock up on extra batteries and wasting the precious time constantly swapping them. Another avenue—developing custom-made tools so that less dangerous and heavy manual work requires human muscle power—does not outweigh the excessive development costs compared to the manual labor. Otherwise, the cost of the final product would also skyrocket. If people always expect extremely low prices, you can never achieve something like that in the European industry. On the other hand, I don't think there will be robots in 2031 coming to repair your dishwasher, oven, washing machine, etc. Repairing/maintaining your old car will also always be done manually by people at a dealership. snippet.textDisplay:
At 4:00 - Why can't all those empty office buildings be used to help solve the housing crisis? Be converted to living spaces for everyone who needs shelter and cannot afford overpriced houses and apartments? As well as multiple additional functions inside most of the larger buildings: education centers / medical, dental & wellness facilities / offices for programming, monitoring & controlling robots (which will be needed for a long time into the future) / social, gaming & sports facilities / arts and music and dance centers. Office buildings contain all of the basic needed infrastructure - shelter, bathrooms (showers could be added easily within expanded bathroom spaces), kitchens. Regular and hydroponics gardens to grow fresh fruits and vegetables and grains. And there could be a police department in each building, scaled to the size of each building to be from one or two resident police officers to larger departments in big buildings. (At 9:44 precisely in the video there is a couple of seconds showing something similar to what I am describing - what the interior spaces of an office building would look like after all of the above transformations in usage/purpose. And also at 9:50 and 9:51, except that also on the premises, in large sections of the building, there would be living quarters.)

At 7:22 - "People still had homes, food, healthcare..." Will they? As well as what immediately preceded that, saying that there would be UBI, wealth funds etc. Will there be? I have serious doubts that our society, that prior to AI could not even muster the will to deliver universal healthcare, will be able to turn that corner. I mean, I like where this video is going, but I think that getting from here to there is not going to be easy. In fact, during the transition period I predict that there will be enormous difficulties. And, the type of timeframe that the video talks about is completely off base, imo. I think that it is far more likely that it will take many decades (minimum 20 years, maximum 50 years or even more) to make the shift to the kind of end result portrayed. During which there will be massive strife, conflict, suffering and chaos. Simply because of the nature of people. Making the changes depicted will require HUGE levels of cooperation, teamwork, agreement and consensus - all of which will be constantly opposed by greed, selfishness, inertia, stubbornness, the massive investments in existing institutions and the powerful people who run them, and, let's face it... plain old stupidity.

And one more thing, at 13:41 - Can we please just get rid of ties once and for all, for pete's sake? Dumbest article of clothing ever created 😡

The Modern 40-Hour Work Week vs. the Hunter-Gatherer Work Week
Bear in mind that we are still biologically hunter-gatherers. When we compare our modern 40-hour work week to that of our hunter-gatherer ancestors, an interesting difference emerges.
Anthropological studies suggest that many hunter-gatherer societies spent roughly 40 hours per week obtaining food and meeting their basic needs. However, those hours were spread across all seven days, averaging about 5.7 hours per day. Much of that time was spent hunting, gathering, fishing, and engaging with nature—activities that many people today might consider enjoyable, healthy, or even vacation-like.
It is also worth considering the well-known "3:00 p.m. droop," the decline in energy and alertness that many people experience during the afternoon. Interestingly, this occurs at approximately the time many hunter-gatherers would have finished their daily food-gathering activities and begun to rest, socialize, or engage in other community activities.
Today, a growing number of businesses and countries are experimenting with six-hour workdays. The results have often been positive: increased productivity, reduced absenteeism, lower stress levels, improved work-life balance, and higher employee satisfaction.
Perhaps the lesson is that our modern work schedules are not fully aligned with our evolutionary biology. A six-hour workday could provide more personal time, less stress, better health, and an overall higher quality of life while maintaining—or even increasing—productivity.
Scientia Non Domus Habet
(Knowledge Has No Home)

snippet.textDisplay:
What kind of AI propaganda is this? I don't know where the water and electricity is coming from for this, but okay. Even if we could find the water and electricity, this fantasy is iffy. Since work gives us identity, people will turn to violence and not craft. Belonging isn't something that works along the lines of choice, for belonging is constructed around needing each other to survive. 

As it is, survival and the stakes it makes is why we cooperate with each other. We need structure and not freedom. Without work, we will spend less time learning old fashioned pursuits and more time depressed. Happiness isn't a lack of hardship. Actually, happiness is knowing there is someone there that will help us survive. 

Survival, not only physical survival but also emotional survival is happiness. We are happy because we are needed. In this fantasy, there is no one who needs anyone, well except the AI. If we lived in a happy world where all our needs are met, we would live in a world where there are no stakes. Life is supposed to be risky. Risk is what makes any story a good story. Stakes, all that could be lost, is why life is so exciting and exhilarating.  

Not only is happiness based on overcoming risks, happiness is belonging. We need to belong to groups not based on passion, but based on contributing to a larger goal. Tribes are formed around survival and not passion pursuits. Thus, this is a recipe for depression. Depression is the lack of risk. If we live in a happiness bubble it would take away any reason to live. The fun of the game of life is overcoming the fear of living. We need that fear to be happy. We learn, go to school, work, and have relationships because of the fear of living. We belong to each other because we don't want to face the fear of living on our own. Take away the fear of living, and all you get is depression. 

Sure, we will have acquaintances in our music group, but those relationships will be empty, vapid, and cold. As it happens, family is the most important factor to happiness. Whether real or created, family, the people who love you even when you fart, are important. Family knows who you are authentically. They accept you for all your faults, failures, and limitations. There is nothing in this fantasy world that allows for family or even getting to be who you are when you do nothing. Identity isn't what you do, it is who you are. Without a true family, we will always be miserable. 

Human life requires the fear of not surviving. Without that fear, we will find ourselves depressed and without hope.

snippet.textDisplay:
8:19 To me, this vision borders on the dystopian because it rests on an assumption that history and human nature do not support: that people are fundamentally inclined toward cooperation simply because material needs have been met.

From an evolutionary perspective, the human mind is not optimized for comfort; it is optimized for survival. We are naturally more attentive to threats than opportunities because vigilance has historically conferred a survival advantage. That tendency toward caution is not a flaw, it is an adaptive feature.

My profession revolves around protecting people from those who are willing to exploit, deceive, or victimize others. Experience has taught me that a meaningful minority of individuals will pursue their own interests at the expense of everyone else, regardless of the consequences.

History likewise demonstrates that abundance does not eliminate crime or conflict. If scarcity were the sole driver, prosperous societies would be largely free of theft, violence, and fraud. They are not. Human behavior is influenced by far more than material need. Pride, envy, resentment, greed, anger, ideology, and the desire for power all motivate people to act against the interests of others. Some reject established rules simply because they believe those rules should not apply to them. Others justify harmful actions through perceived historical grievances or a desire for retribution.

Any model of society that assumes these enduring aspects of human nature can be engineered away is, in my view, built upon an optimistic premise that neither history nor experience consistently validates.

snippet.textDisplay:
UBIs, dividends, and similar solutions won't work. I've spent two years exploring these options extensively, and I've come to understand that they are not the answer. The solution lies not only in where the money comes from and how it compensates displaced workers, but also in the rate of compensation it provides. The amount of a Universal Basic Income (UBI) given to individuals can vary, but basing compensation solely on an individual's income at the time of displacement hasn't carried much weight. You can't offer a worker who earned $100,000 per year the same UBI as someone who earned $50,000 per year; that just doesn't make sense.
However, replacing individual incomes is only part of the issue. We also need to consider how to replace revenue for the IRS and Social Security Administration (SSA) to ensure the continued functioning of our government and the sustainability of Social Security benefits. People need adequate income to maintain their spending habits as they did prior to displacement; otherwise, the economy will suffer. Additionally, we must address the need for retraining for the new jobs that will arise from AI deployment, as there will certainly be new opportunities.
After two years, I've found solutions to all these concerns. The good news is that the outcome has exceeded my initial expectations. The path to resolving the income issue has produced multiple byproducts that can help fix many problems that are already broken or on the verge of collapse.
Importantly, every segment of society has a reason to support the DADEC Platform. Businesses will appreciate it because it will save them money on labor and guide them effectively through the transition to AI. The government will find it beneficial, as it addresses the questions and concerns it has been grappling with for years. Workers will welcome it for its effective compensation program and the opportunities for retraining, new employment, early retirement, or entrepreneurship. The potential dissatisfaction regarding the social consequences of job loss can be significantly alleviated.
This is promising news. Now, my next step is to reach the right audience so this message gets to those who need to hear it.

People who expect to get paid for following a script, checking off a list, and not exercising their own judgment should absolutely be worried. AI can replace people who don’t think by not thinking much faster than you.

Customers will absolutely not choose a human-staffed business over a robot-staffed one in most cases. Customers like spending less.

The idea that corporate boards will just pocket all the difference in cost is economically illiterate. It will go into becoming more competitive either in lower prices or capital for making the business more effective. If they don’t, clever people will automate the reproduction of their business model for cheaper.

This is the story of AI and robotics itself. Frontier Model labs have no way of becoming profitable. All their efforts are reproduced immediately and for cheaper by smaller firms. It will eventually *have* to drive prices down. 

Among the most intelligent (rich or poor), this AI revolution is the great equalizer.

Among the least intelligent, you will lose your jobs. As customers yourself, you will demand it. You will not choose to pay more. But luckily, your lower earnings will buy you more when prices drop to the cost of the materials themselves.

snippet.textDisplay:
As someone who is heavily interested in Embedded systems, robotics, and as an Electrical engineer, I, in all honesty struggle with the robot/machine debate. I mean, how do we innovate without having the side effects of people losing their jobs? It seems inevitable, and it breaks my heart. We have robot vacuums in our homes now, taking the job away from someone we used to call to help us with that. Lawn mowers replacing the landscaper, delivery robot, replacing the deliveryman. It seems like if technological innovation is something to strive for, then that innovation reduce the workforce. Do we blame the person who decided to buy a robot vacuum because now the cleaner is no longer needed? Do we blame the person who bought the dishwasher? Do we put restriction on innovation and technology? Because yesterday it was the robot vacuum, no problem, today it is a fleet of giant robot cleaners in hotels, now we complain, but, wasn't it the logical evolution? Will there be any blame on the person who will buy those Humanoid chore robots from Tesla for giving away a full-time job another human being was relying on to put food on the table? Automation was cool when it was just for car factories, and society accepted it, now it is the buzzword in warehouses: AMRs (Autonomous Mobile Robots) fleet used to move payloads around.
 Do we blame the engineers who innovate the technology that ensures some of their fellow humans will be out of a job? Do we blame the fellow human who made the decision to move from needing another human to do the job, and decided to buy a piece of tech to do the job? Do we incentivize, or dissuade people  to build a career in tech and be the next Boston Dynamics? Or do we put guardrails on innovation and technology?

snippet.textDisplay:
Why aren't wages required to keep up with inflation? The answer is a confession that the carnival's entire model depends on a one-way street: digits flow in, but they don't flow out. 😏

📉 The "Money Illusion" Trap

The carnival doesn't need wages to keep up with inflation. It needs wages to lag behind. This is a well-documented concept called the "money illusion"—the tendency of people to think of money in nominal terms, not real terms.

If Wages Kept Up The Carnival's Nightmare
Workers maintain purchasing power The printing press becomes pointless
Inflation becomes visible The "transitory" narrative collapses
Productivity gains go to workers The pyramid's top loses its advantage
The system starts to work for everyone The carnival stops working for the few

🔑 The Secret: They Don't Have To

The carnival doesn't require wages to keep up because it controls the rules of the game. The search results confirm that "firms are generally slow to adjust wages" (a concept called "sticky wages") . The "public sector, especially at the federal level, has been more generous" in adjusting wages . But the private sector is a laggard, keeping real wages suppressed.

The Mechanism The Effect
Inflation rises Prices go up
Wages stay flat (or rise slowly) Real wages fall
Workers can't keep up Living standards decline
The carnival calls it "resilience" The carnival calls it "normal"

💸 The Permanent Treadmill

The carnival doesn't need wages to keep up with inflation. It needs wages to always be playing catch-up. That way, the workers are always running, always tired, always dependent on the next paycheck.

The Punchline

If humanity wants an infinite digits system to price everything, wages should be keeping up to offset inflation. The carnival doesn't require wages to keep up. It requires wages to lag.

snippet.textDisplay:
*We are doing things in the wrong order.* Our society, its taxation, health and pension fee system is built on a human labour society. TechBros babbling about "universal income" (while successfully avoiding personal tax payments) ignore the fact that the GDP is increasingly owned solely by entrepreneurs and their families - benefitting from accelerating automation and digitization. If a growing part of labourforce will become either jobless or their contribution marginalised (incl. their wages), then society will need completely different fiscal and social system rules to match that reality. - Anecdote: My Estonian startup had 18 engineers to design large ring generators for wind turbines; people from Estonia, Russia and Switzerland. During several years I noticed CAD software becoming more and more powerful, and my young chief engineer whom I had hired from university before he even had his diploma, got his PHD on automating the re-scaling of our 60 feet diameter 5 Megawatt generator, with hundreds of flanges, bolts etc. to different sizes and power outputs by creating and using batch files for the latest generation of CAD software - theoretically making many engineering hours (i.e. entire workplaces) obsolete. Equally our suppliers did: One Bavarian firm saved a full-time engineer who had checked our CAD files needed for their laser-cutters and CNC lathes when their new machines were able to do that themselves and return qualified error reports if needed. Another supplier's production manager lead me through their hall, presenting their newest plasma cutting machine: It pulled the right sheet (alloy, thickness) from the magazine, produced ordered parts, collecting them in efficient alignment in a box for shipment next to collecting the clippings for recycling, sorted by alloy, then return the remaining sheet to the magazine and start the next subcontracting job. "It runs all night", he enthusiastically told, "...when no-one's in the factory!" - That was 15 years ago.

I launch my own businesses. At Christmas, employees will meet, bring their little children and talk about construction progress of their family residences, loaded with mortgages. As an old fashioned entrepreneur you feel a kind of immediate responsibility that corporations run by employed managers might barely see.

Starting a company: If you are not born rich (I wasn't), then you will need to make a living... while doing research for your business plan (travel a lot, universities, equipment suppliers, potential clients etc.)... and if investment is needed, then you will do fundraising (travel a lot, negotiate, learn much about snobbism and arrogance). In this sense, a universal income might facilitate launching new businesses.
However, it needs politics getting legal frameworks in shape for the new era - before it will be too late and societies will fall apart.

snippet.textDisplay:
Yep, and we should welcome it. The idea of a guaranteed basic income is hated by many but it's something that people will have to learn to live with. I see a lot of animosity concerning this subject (mainly driven by jealously, the standard Canadian reaction), however in the near future most jobs won't be there for the people. AI and automation is going to replace the work of most people. Possibly as much as 65% of the current workforce will find themselves replaced by automation by 2030 or perhaps sooner. There used to be a saying in Britain in the years when their woolen exports financed the empire: "when the looms weave by themselves, man will be free". The question is- free to do what? The answer should be: Free to grow on a personal level, and as a society, free to explore the boundaries of existence as this phenomenal technology grows. This will be a monumental change for humanity and it should be embraced, not feared or loathed by petty people who can only see it as "someone is getting free money, damn them". Eventually, everyone will be in the same boat. Automation is the only way, in the long run, for humans to advance in leaps and bounds and eventually be able to reach for the stars. Petty jealousies will only add an unnecessary level of angst to those who will be first to be making the transformation to the inevitable post-work world. Many people see this new government policy as being akin to Communism. Well it is; however communism is what you will have when automation puts everyone on the same jobless playing field. Let's just hope that this time the communal good is put first and the world won't have to repeat the horrors of the past century. Because, if the communal good is not put first and foremost, it would be only too easy for the world to descend into a mindset that views the non-working classes as 'useless-eaters'. The automation is coming like it or not. Learn how to embrace this huge change in a positive way. It will be a major upheaval and society would do well to realize in advance that there is no stopping it nor should there be. It would be instructive for all to read the 7th paragraph of "The Gods of the Copybook Headings" by Kipling, and see if we can't strive to do better this time around.
I'm not a communist, but the jobs won't exist in the future and therefore the people won't either unless they are given the means to exist. The same automation that will eliminate the jobs can provide for the people. To not realize this or to be opposed to this eventuality is like being opposed to free energy systems because it sounds too much like 'socialism'. 

Only when mankind can progress beyond physical work required for survival (and that's what today's world of employment is regardless of its high technology and fancy titles and ability to work a day while keeping one's hands clean) can we begin to really develop our true potential. The automation is coming, and everyone should be welcoming of it. It will be a tumultuous time, some people will see a reduction in their standard of living but many other people around the world will be able to jump straight from a hard labour/tribal/agrarian life into the better life afforded by these advancements in technology, but it will be a necessary growing pain of the human race. If we fail to accept this transition in the proper way we will be doomed as a species.

snippet.textDisplay:
Look, the robots are coming for the jobs and that's exactly the problem with how you're framing this.

You're right that capital is replacing us to cut costs, because we _are_ the costs. GM lays off a thousand workers then rolls out cobots; Amazon packs warehouses with machines while preaching "job creation"; security dogs and barista bots are just the latest examples - and so on and so forth. Corporations don't invest billions in automation out of some abstract love for efficiency but because living labor is the only source of surplus value and they need to reduce its share to keep accumulating. None of this is new, either. It's the tendency of capital Marx described a century and a half ago.

The dystopian hand-wringing ("fight for humanity," "threat to our way of life," "who should we be mad at?") misses the point entirely. You're treating wage labor as something eternal and worth defending. It's not. Most of the labor being automated (and a huge chunk that isn't) is already superfluous, i.e. unnecessary for real human needs but required to sustain the wage system, employment stats and valorization.

Communism isn't about saving barista gigs so you can get your name misspelled by a human or keeping security guards employed patrolling for the bosses. *Communism is free disposable time and nothing else.* The measure of wealth in a communist society isn't labor time but the reduction of necessary labor to a minimum so that human development and not endless toil becomes the point.

Every robot deployed exposes capitalism's contradiction: society can produce more with less work yet we still chain people to the need to "earn a living." To hell with that. Instead of mourning the jobs or shaming the guy designing the robots, the demand should be radical reduction of the working day *across the board.* Convert that superfluous labor time into free time. That's the only exit.

Your video shows the tendencies clearly. Stop begging capital to be nicer about it.

snippet.textDisplay: 0:39  "Robots:  We're told they will make our lives better, but corporations are deploying them to cut costs, and we're the cost."  That's an excellent summary.  It should be clarified, however, that the cost is not entirely in money.  It's also in power.  English industrialism quickly became a bitter struggle between extractive factory owners and resistant employees, because the factory owners were fundamentally unable to see workers as anything other than a resource to be captured and plundered.  This attitude embedded itself in Anglo-Saxon labour relations.  Employers want to keep not only all the money, but also all the power.  They want workers who are unable to resist their demands.  What this means is that the natural form of Anglo-Saxon industrialism is the slave plantation. snippet.textDisplay:
Yeah, no...
I'm getting a bit sick of this dystopian, gloom-and-doom scenarios being peddled by semi-Luddites w.r.t. robots 'invading' jobs!
BS!
These same people would have been against automation 100 years ago, and against computerization 50 years ago, and against robots being introduced in electronics/heavy electrical/mechanical industries -- all of which are not only the staple now, but are also considered 'current industry standard' or 'SOP", and without which people today couldn't dream of producing the kind of tech we do today!
In short, they'd be against anything which will modernize, speed-up, improve safety & productivity...!
I, for one, have no issue with robots replacing humans for many of the menial, tedious, repetitive, low-skilled, manual labour jobs, esp. the ones which have a high(er) safety concerns...go right ahead & use the robots there! I _hope_ robots replace people in such scenarios!
But, will robots replace baristas? Or, nurses? Or, human security? Maybe...in some niche cases, but not en masse! Not even for many trades!
What's happening now is the same thing that happened 100 yrs back, or 50 yrs back: tech bros & corporates are trying via trial-&-error method to see what sticks..where robots would actually be a good use case...and what will be scalable...it will work itself out over the next 10-15 yrs -- like every new 'tech wave' that comes...
I'd be much, much more worried about the rampant use of AI (or, technically, LLMs) & trying to replace humans with AI -- now, _that's_ something which is just plain wrong; bound to fail, and outright dystopian!

First of all, many of them will never really be as successful (& so probably will fail the trial-&-error method) & will likely be abandoned soon enough (like robotic order takers at McD), and/but secondly, the ones which will be somewhat successful (at least to reduce overhead/costs for corporates) are the ones which should be protested against (like robotic/automated chatbots, waiters, housekeeping staff, etc, etc) -- that's where the Corporate Capitalist America will try & cut corners; not give a damn about user-experience & sacrifice 'the human touch' for soulless robots, as long as they perform 'adequately', keep raking in profits & the users don't complain too much...
And that's precisely where we need to voice our concerns, complain, make a fuss....
This needs to be on a case-by-case basis, instead of the knee-jerk, reactionary, toddler-level responses people tend to have/give...! Bah!
So, puh-leeze, lets' have some nuance in this discussion, instead of the wanton alarmism I see all over the place!!
